Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Regency of Banyuwangi. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration. 3. Regional Head is the Regent of Banyuwangi. 4. SKPD in charge of Women Empowerment and Child Protection is the Regional Apparatus Organization that has the main duties and functions in the field of women empowerment and child protection in the Regency of Banyuwangi. 5. Woman is a person who is female. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb. 7. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harbouring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within a country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 8. Rights of the child are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the state. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological matters that causes danger to life, body, or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in physical, mental, social, psychosocial, and sexual suffering of children. 11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or to a person's body, miscarriage and/or unconsciousness and/or causes death. 12. Psychological Violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, coercion of sexual intercourse, coercion of sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, coercion of sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Victim is a woman including female workers working abroad and children who experience suffering and/or hardship either directly or indirectly as a result of such suffering. 15. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent that includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical, sexual exploitation, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 16. Sexual exploitation is any form of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and obscenity. 17. Recruitment is an act that includes inviting, gathering, bringing, or separating a person from their family or community. 18. Transfer is an act of dispatching or landing a person from one place to another place. 19. Debt bondage is an act of placing a person in a status or condition of pledging or being forced to pledge themselves or their family or people for whom they are responsible or their personal services as a form of debt repayment. 20. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing security in the fulfillment of their rights by giving consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 21. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and the fulfillment of their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from acts of violence and discrimination. 22. Service is an action carried out as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against the victim is or has occurred. 23. Companion is a person who has the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Social worker is a person who has the expertise to listen empathetically and explore problems to provide counseling in efforts to strengthen the psychological condition of victims. 25. Commission for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter referred to as KPPA, is an institution that handles the protection of women and children whose membership consists of relevant agencies, NGOs and Academics. 26. Medicolegal is an effort to collect evidence for the purpose of proof in the judicial process. 27. Women Crisis Center is a service center for women and children victims of violence. 28. Safe house is a temporary residence for victims, in order to obtain security and not be reached by the perpetrator or the perpetrator's agent, as long as the case has not been resolved. 29. Restitution is the payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs. 30. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 31. Reintegration is the process of reuniting victims with their family, or substitute family and community supported by providing educational assistance or skills enhancement and assistance. 32. Standard Operating Procedure, hereinafter referred to as SPO, is a procedure that becomes a reference for service actions established by Regent's Decree. 33.

1. Region is the Regency of Banyuwangi. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration. 3. Regional Head is the Regent of Banyuwangi. 4. Woman is a person who is female. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb. 7. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harbouring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within a country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 8. Rights of the child are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the state. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological matters that causes danger to life, body, or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in physical, mental, social, psychosocial, and sexual suffering of children. 11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or to a person's body, miscarriage and/or unconsciousness and/or causes death. 12. Psychological Violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, coercion of sexual intercourse, coercion of sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, coercion of sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Sexual exploitation is any form of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and obscenity. 17. Transfer is an act of dispatching or landing a person from one place to another place. 19. CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE AND HUMAN TRAFFICKING

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children including human trafficking has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence are general, having no relevance to the level of education, occupation, and income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection with social status, religion and beliefs, as well as particular ethnicities, ethnic groups, or races. One of the causes is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed and manifested in social life.

That violence and human trafficking that has occurred so far is like the iceberg theory, meaning that cases recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.

According to reports from the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and the Indonesian Child Mitigation Network (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore, firm law enforcement is necessary, because in addition to the state, the Regional Government also has the obligation and responsibility to prevent and sanction acts of trafficking in women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, healing and compensation to victims of violations.

Thus it is expected that the main objective of the drafting of this Regional Regulation Draft can be achieved well, namely to provide a legal basis for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Human Trafficking as well as ensure the implementation of the regional government's obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and eradicating violence and trafficking.

II. ELUCIDATION ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Discrimination against women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women; 34. Integrated Service Center for Women Empowerment and Child, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the government or community-based, which includes: referral center, business consultation center, reproductive health consultation center, legal consultation center, integrated crisis center (PKT), integrated service center (PPT), trauma recovery center (trauma center), women's crisis management center (women crisis center), training center, safe house (shelter), transit house, or other forms. 35. Community organization is an organization formed by members of Indonesian citizens voluntarily on the basis of shared vision, mission, profession, function and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, consisting of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other organizational forms. 36. Accompanying institution is an institution that provides assistance to women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons in the Regency of Banyuwangi. 37. Empathy is a mental condition that makes a person feel themselves in the same state of feeling or thought with a person or group who is a victim of violence and trafficking in persons.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

SKPD in charge of Women Empowerment and Child Protection is the Regional Apparatus Organization that has the main duties and functions in the field of women empowerment and child protection in the Regency of Banyuwangi. 5. Woman is a person who is female. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb. 7. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harbouring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within a country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 8. Rights of the child are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the state. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological matters that causes danger to life, body, or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in physical, mental, social, psychosocial, and sexual suffering of children. 11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or to a person's body, miscarriage and/or unconsciousness and/or causes death. 12. Psychological Violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 13. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent that includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical, sexual exploitation, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 16. Transfer is an act of dispatching or landing a person from one place to another place. 19. CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE AND HUMAN TRAFFICKING

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children including human trafficking has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence are general, having no relevance to the level of education, occupation, and income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection with social status, religion and beliefs, as well as particular ethnicities, ethnic groups, or races. One of the causes is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed and manifested in social life.

That violence and human trafficking that has occurred so far is like the iceberg theory, meaning that cases recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.

According to reports from the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and the Indonesian Child Mitigation Network (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore, firm law enforcement is necessary, because in addition to the state, the Regional Government also has the obligation and responsibility to prevent and sanction acts of trafficking in women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, healing and compensation to victims of violations.

Thus it is expected that the main objective of the drafting of this Regional Regulation Draft can be achieved well, namely to provide a legal basis for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Human Trafficking as well as ensure the implementation of the regional government's obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and eradicating violence and trafficking.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE AND HUMAN TRAFFICKING

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children including human trafficking has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence are general, having no relevance to the level of education, occupation, and income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection with social status, religion and beliefs, as well as particular ethnicities, ethnic groups, or races. One of the causes is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed and manifested in social life.

That violence and human trafficking that has occurred so far is like the iceberg theory, meaning that cases recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.

According to reports from the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and the Indonesian Child Mitigation Network (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore, firm law enforcement is necessary, because in addition to the state, the Regional Government also has the obligation and responsibility to prevent and sanction acts of trafficking in women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, healing and compensation to victims of violations.

Thus it is expected that the main objective of the drafting of this Regional Regulation Draft can be achieved well, namely to provide a legal basis for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Human Trafficking as well as ensure the implementation of the regional government's obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and eradicating violence and trafficking.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children including human trafficking has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence are general, having no relevance to the level of education, occupation, and income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection with social status, religion and beliefs, as well as particular ethnicities, ethnic groups, or races. One of the causes is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed and manifested in social life.

That violence and human trafficking that has occurred so far is like the iceberg theory, meaning that cases recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.

According to reports from the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and the Indonesian Child Mitigation Network (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore, firm law enforcement is necessary, because in addition to the state, the Regional Government also has the obligation and responsibility to prevent and sanction acts of trafficking in women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, healing and compensation to victims of violations.

Thus it is expected that the main objective of the drafting of this Regional Regulation Draft can be achieved well, namely to provide a legal basis for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Human Trafficking as well as ensure the implementation of the regional government's obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and eradicating violence and trafficking.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE AND HUMAN TRAFFICKING

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children including human trafficking has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence are general, having no relevance to the level of education, occupation, and income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection with social status, religion and beliefs, as well as particular ethnicities, ethnic groups, or races. One of the causes is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed and manifested in social life.

That violence and human trafficking that has occurred so far is like the iceberg theory, meaning that cases recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.

According to reports from the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and the Indonesian Child Mitigation Network (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore, firm law enforcement is necessary, because in addition to the state, the Regional Government also has the obligation and responsibility to prevent and sanction acts of trafficking in women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, healing and compensation to victims of violations.

Thus it is expected that the main objective of the drafting of this Regional Regulation Draft can be achieved well, namely to provide a legal basis for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Human Trafficking as well as ensure the implementation of the regional government's obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and eradicating violence and trafficking.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Regency of Banyuwangi. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration. 3. Regional Head is the Regent of Banyuwangi. 4. SKPD in charge of Women Empowerment and Child Protection is the Regional Apparatus Organization that has the main duties and functions in the field of women empowerment and child protection in the Regency of Banyuwangi. 5. Woman is a person who is female. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb. 7. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harbouring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within a country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 8. Rights of the child are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the state. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological matters that causes danger to life, body, or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in physical, mental, social, psychosocial, and sexual suffering of children. 11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or to a person's body, miscarriage and/or unconsciousness and/or causes death. 12. Psychological Violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, coercion of sexual intercourse, coercion of sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, coercion of sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Victim is a woman including female workers working abroad and children who experience suffering and/or hardship either directly or indirectly as a result of such suffering. 15. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent that includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical, sexual exploitation, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 16. Sexual exploitation is any form of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and obscenity. 17. Recruitment is an act that includes inviting, gathering, bringing, or separating a person from their family or community. 18. Transfer is an act of dispatching or landing a person from one place to another place. 19. Debt bondage is an act of placing a person in a status or condition of pledging or being forced to pledge themselves or their family or people for whom they are responsible or their personal services as a form of debt repayment. 20. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing security in the fulfillment of their rights by giving consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 21. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and the fulfillment of their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from acts of violence and discrimination. 22. Service is an action carried out as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against the victim is or has occurred. 23. Companion is a person who has the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Social worker is a person who has the expertise to listen empathetically and explore problems to provide counseling in efforts to strengthen the psychological condition of victims. 25. Commission for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter referred to as KPPA, is an institution that handles the protection of women and children whose membership consists of relevant agencies, NGOs and Academics. 26. Medicolegal is an effort to collect evidence for the purpose of proof in the judicial process. 27. Women Crisis Center is a service center for women and children victims of violence. 28. Safe house is a temporary residence for victims, in order to obtain security and not be reached by the perpetrator or the perpetrator's agent, as long as the case has not been resolved. 29. Restitution is the payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs. 30. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 31. Reintegration is the process of reuniting victims with their family, or substitute family and community supported by providing educational assistance or skills enhancement and assistance. 32. Standard Operating Procedure, hereinafter referred to as SPO, is a procedure that becomes a reference for service actions established by Regent's Decree. 33.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Regency of Banyuwangi. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration. 3. Regional Head is the Regent of Banyuwangi. 4. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harbouring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within a country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 8. Rights of the child are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the state. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological matters that causes danger to life, body, or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or to a person's body, miscarriage and/or unconsciousness and/or causes death. 12. Psychological Violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 13. (1) To ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children who are victims of violence and human trafficking, the Regency Government conducts monitoring.

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE AND HUMAN TRAFFICKING

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The practice of exploitation and violence against women and children including human trafficking has recently continued to increase in number. Perpetrators of exploitation and violence are general, having no relevance to the level of education, occupation, and income. Perpetrators of violence also have no connection with social status, religion and beliefs, as well as particular ethnicities, ethnic groups, or races. One of the causes is the patriarchal cultural factor that views women as lower than men. Violence against women and children can and will continue to occur as long as the imbalance in the relationship between men and women is still believed and manifested in social life.

That violence and human trafficking that has occurred so far is like the iceberg theory, meaning that cases recorded and reported are only the number on the surface, while far below the surface there are more that are not recorded and not reached by assistance nor receive serious attention from the authorities.

According to reports from the American Center for International Labor Solidarity (ACILS) and the Indonesian Child Mitigation Network (JARAK), specifically for East Java Province, areas that are vulnerable and potential for women and child trafficking are Banyuwangi, Malang, Blitar, Tulungagung, and Trenggalek. Therefore, firm law enforcement is necessary, because in addition to the state, the Regional Government also has the obligation and responsibility to prevent and sanction acts of trafficking in women and children, as well as provide protection, assistance, healing and compensation to victims of violations.

Thus it is expected that the main objective of the drafting of this Regional Regulation Draft can be achieved well, namely to provide a legal basis for efforts to protect Women and Children Victims of Violence and Human Trafficking as well as ensure the implementation of the regional government's obligations in carrying out the mandate of laws and regulations in preventing and eradicating violence and trafficking.

II. ELUCIDATION ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 20

(1) In implementing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children who are victims of violence and human trafficking, the regency government may cooperate with international institutions.

(2) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Regency of Banyuwangi. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of regional government administration. 3. Regional Head is the Regent of Banyuwangi. 4. SKPD in charge of Women Empowerment and Child Protection is the Regional Apparatus Organization that has the main duties and functions in the field of women empowerment and child protection in the Regency of Banyuwangi. 5. Woman is a person who is female. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb. 7. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harbouring, transfer, relocation, or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage, or giving payments or benefits to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within a country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 8. Rights of the child are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the state. 9. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological matters that causes danger to life, body, or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom. 10. Violence against children is any act that results in or may result in physical, mental, social, psychosocial, and sexual suffering of children. 11. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or to a person's body, miscarriage and/or unconsciousness and/or causes death. 12. Psychological Violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 13. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, coercion of sexual intercourse, coercion of sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, coercion of sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 14. Victim is a woman including female workers working abroad and children who experience suffering and/or hardship either directly or indirectly as a result of such suffering. 15. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent that includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical, sexual exploitation, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 16. Sexual exploitation is any form of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution and obscenity. 17. Recruitment is an act that includes inviting, gathering, bringing, or separating a person from their family or community. 18. Transfer is an act of dispatching or landing a person from one place to another place. 19. Debt bondage is an act of placing a person in a status or condition of pledging or being forced to pledge themselves or their family or people for whom they are responsible or their personal services as a form of debt repayment. 20. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing security in the fulfillment of their rights by giving consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 21. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and the fulfillment of their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from acts of violence and discrimination. 22. Service is an action carried out as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against the victim is or has occurred. 23. Companion is a person who has the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence. 24. Social worker is a person who has the expertise to listen empathetically and explore problems to provide counseling in efforts to strengthen the psychological condition of victims. 25. Commission for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter referred to as KPPA, is an institution that handles the protection of women and children whose membership consists of relevant agencies, NGOs and Academics. 26. Medicolegal is an effort to collect evidence for the purpose of proof in the judicial process. 27. Women Crisis Center is a service center for women and children victims of violence. 28. Safe house is a temporary residence for victims, in order to obtain security and not be reached by the perpetrator or the perpetrator's agent, as long as the case has not been resolved. 29. Restitution is the payment of compensation charged to the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by the victim or their heirs. 30. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 31. Reintegration is the process of reuniting victims with their family, or substitute family and community supported by providing educational assistance or skills enhancement and assistance. 32. Standard Operating Procedure, hereinafter referred to as SPO, is a procedure that becomes a reference for service actions established by Regent's Decree. 33.

Discrimination against women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women; 34. Integrated Service Center for Women Empowerment and Child, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the government or community-based, which includes: referral center, business consultation center, reproductive health consultation center, legal consultation center, integrated crisis center (PKT), integrated service center (PPT), trauma recovery center (trauma center), women's crisis management center (women crisis center), training center, safe house (shelter), transit house, or other forms. 35. Community organization is an organization formed by members of Indonesian citizens voluntarily on the basis of shared vision, mission, profession, function and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, consisting of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other organizational forms. 36. Accompanying institution is an institution that provides assistance to women and children victims of violence and trafficking in persons in the Regency of Banyuwangi. 37. Empathy is a mental condition that makes a person feel themselves in the same state of feeling or thought with a person or group who is a victim of violence and trafficking in persons.

Article 9

(1) The system for implementing protection for victims of trafficking in persons and violence against women and children is carried out through 2 (two) methods, namely:

a. Preventive or prevention method; and
b. Repressive or handling method
(2) The preventive or prevention method is carried out through various forms of protection, both by the community and the government, which are intended to prevent the occurrence of criminal acts of trafficking in persons and violence or victims of violence against women and children.
(3) The repressive or handling method is carried out through various forms of protection carried out by the government through regulatory, implementation and enforcement activities of legislation governing the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons.
(4) Guidelines and Technical Procedures for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence and Trafficking in Persons are further regulated through Regent Regulation.
